- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift (increasing trend) while true outcomes often exhibit sharp downward corrections or mean reversion.
- After price spikes (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct, leading to overprediction in subsequent days.
- Model underestimates true volatility in the second half of the 30d window, particularly when prices drop sharply.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture sudden drops or spikes in true outcomes.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., <80), model tends to underestimate and then slowly recover, missing sharp rebounds.
- Model overconfident in upward trend — fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven downward pressure (e.g., EU ETS cap adjustments).
